title: Bi Sheng invents clay movable type
summary: Bi Sheng, who lived in Northern Song China, is credited with inventing movable-type printing, carving each character on a clay block and firing it hard, around 1045 and in the Qingli reign (1041–1048). The earliest surviving account is in Shen Kuo's Dream Pool Essays, written after Shen retired about 1088. The invention was not widely adopted in his time.

uncertainty.note: Sources give the Qingli reign (1041–1048) and c. 1045; the queue id year 1040 is not supported by either page.

where.modern_name: Yingshan County, Huanggang, Hubei, China (where his tomb shows he lived; place of invention not stated)
where.historical_name: Northern Song China; Yingshan County is the place the sources link to him, no historical name given

importance.justification: EBSCO calls it the first movable type, about four centuries before Gutenberg, though not widely adopted in his time.

reviewer_note: Least sure of the pin: neither page says where the type was made. EBSCO says his tomb shows he lived in Yingshan County, Hubei, so the pin is that county (GeoNames, 300 km uncertainty). The queue id says 1040, but both pages give c. 1045 or 1041–1048; Berkshire lists his years as 990–1052 while EBSCO cites a tombstone death date of 1051, so no life dates are given.
